# Results — Study 935 (Value Averaging) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). $1 a month for **36 months**
into **SPY**, two ways: a fixed amount every month (DCA) versus trading to Edleson's
**value path** (VA). Both arms are handed **identical committed capital** — a pre-funded
**6-month** cash buffer plus the same contribution schedule — idle money earns **BIL**'s
actual total return, and the accounts are compared on **whole-account terminal wealth**
(shares plus cash). The buffer is finite: when VA demands more than is there the purchase
is **capped** and the shortfall recorded. One execution lag (order sized at the decision
month-end close, filled at the next day's close), 1 bp one-way on traded notional, no
shorting and therefore no borrow. Daily total-return closes (`yfinance`,
`auto_adjust=True`). Common SPY∩BIL window 2007-05-30 → 2026-06-30 (BIL's inception gates
the tradable cash leg). As-of **2026-06-30** — the partial current month is dropped.
**Survivorship:** the sleeves are index vehicles that survived the whole window and whose
underlying indices are reconstituted, so index-level survivorship is embedded in the level
of **both** arms and cancels in the VA-minus-DCA difference that is the headline here.*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPY (equity sleeve), BIL (cash leg) | 2007-05-30 → 2026-06-30 | 4,802 | Fingerprint `edef65f148a6` |

*The fingerprint hashes the cached **price levels**, and `auto_adjust=True` re-scales the
entire history every time a new dividend lands, so a refresh of the shared cache moves it
even when nothing about the sample has changed. It moved three times during this study's
build and audit (`d92041f54285` → `dd13f1779dbb` → `9cce1b76d021` → `edef65f148a6`) and
**every statistic below was identical to three decimal places across all four** — as it
must be, since the engine is scale-invariant in the sleeve price. Treat the fingerprint as
a provenance stamp on the file, not as a checksum on the result.*

Cross-check sleeves IEF and QQQ are cached in the shared `studies/_cache` too. **193**
rolling programmes, starts 2007-05-31 → 2023-05-31, last valuation 2026-06-01.

## Headline — VA minus DCA terminal wealth, cents per dollar contributed

| Statistic | Value |
|---|--:|
| Mean gap (VA − DCA) | **−1.372c** |
| Median / sd | −1.053c / 2.113c |
| HAC *t* (Newey-West, lag 36) | **−3.87** |
| Non-overlapping *t* (every 36th window, n = 6) | −0.98 |
| Block bootstrap 95% CI (36-window blocks) | **[−2.057, −0.742]** |
| VA win rate | **29.0%**, Wilson [23.1%, 35.8%] |
| Excess-of-cash terminal, per dollar contributed | VA +19.04c vs DCA **+20.41c** |
| Mean equity weight over the programme | VA 0.634 vs DCA **0.699** |
| Dispersion ratio (VA/DCA excess-of-cash sd) | 0.810 |
| Worst / best window | −7.38c (start 2018-12-31) / +2.87c (start 2017-04-28) |

The non-overlapping *t* is quoted for honesty, not power: nineteen years of tape contain
only six independent 36-month programmes.

## The metric that makes value averaging look good

| IRR measure | VA | DCA | VA edge |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **Equity-only** (Edleson's own metric — flows that touch the sleeve) | **14.90%/yr** | 13.97%/yr | **+0.92 pp** |
| **Whole programme** (buffer in, contributions in, total account out) | 10.07%/yr | **10.64%/yr** | −0.57 pp |

The equity-only figure is **near-invariant to the buffer** across the entire 0→24-month
sweep — it moves 18 bp in total while the whole-programme IRR underneath it halves — which
is the tell: it is not measuring the programme the saver runs.

| Buffer | Equity-only IRR VA / DCA | Whole-programme IRR VA / DCA |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 × C | 14.73% / 13.97% | 12.97% / 13.92% |
| 3 × C | 14.87% / 13.97% | 11.35% / 12.03% |
| 6 × C | 14.90% / 13.97% | 10.07% / 10.64% |
| 12 × C | 14.91% / 13.97% | 8.27% / 8.73% |
| 24 × C | 14.91% / 13.97% | 6.22% / 6.56% |

The left column barely moves while the programme underneath it changes completely; the
right column moves with the programme and never favours VA.

## The cash the rule demands

| | |
|---|---|
| Cap binds | **6 / 193 windows (3.1%)** — 14 binding months in total, 0.20% of all rebalance months |
| Binding programme starts | 2007-05, -06, -07, -08, -09, -10 — every one of them into the crisis |
| Worst **single-month** unfunded call | **3.32 × the monthly contribution** |
| Worst **programme-total** shortfall (summed over its binding months) | **6.57 × the monthly contribution** |
| Trades / notional per programme | VA 36 trades, **34.66** notional; DCA 36 trades, 36.00 |
| Cost per dollar contributed | VA 0.0096c vs DCA 0.0100c |

VA trades *less* notional than DCA — its sells net against its buys — so friction cannot
be the explanation for anything here.

## Robustness

**Era cut (window start before / after 2016-01-01)**

| Era | n | Gap | HAC *t* | VA wins | equity VA/DCA |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| starts 2007–2015 | 104 | −1.518c | −2.98 | 23.1% | 0.640 / 0.699 |
| starts 2016–2023 | 89 | −1.201c | −2.50 | 36.0% | 0.628 / 0.698 |

**Sweep: value-path growth rate (an ASSUMPTION, nowhere on the tape)**

| Assumed growth | VA equity weight | Gap | HAC *t* | Cap binds |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0%/yr (Edleson's basic linear path) | 0.634 | **−1.372c** | −3.87 | 3.1% |
| 4%/yr | 0.654 | −0.644c | −2.02 | 3.6% |
| 8%/yr | 0.673 | +0.096c | +0.33 | 3.6% |
| 12%/yr | 0.693 | **+0.834c** | +3.23 | **13.0%** |

The gap tracks the equity weight monotonically and changes sign where the weights meet
DCA's 0.699. The growth rate is not a tuning detail — it is the whole result.

**Sweep: cash buffer (an ASSUMPTION)**

| Buffer | Gap | HAC *t* | Cap binds |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 × C | −1.675c | −5.16 | **86.5%** |
| 3 × C | −1.421c | −4.19 | 6.2% |
| 6 × C | −1.372c | −3.87 | 3.1% |
| 12 × C | −1.346c | −3.69 | 0.0% |
| 24 × C | −1.346c | −3.69 | 0.0% |

**Sweep: one-way cost** — 0 bp −1.372c, 5 bp −1.370c, 25 bp −1.363c (*t* = −3.91). The
gap is *slightly less* negative at higher cost, because DCA trades more notional.

**Sweep: horizon**

| Horizon | n | Gap | HAC *t* | VA wins | equity VA/DCA |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 24 months | 205 | −0.481c | −2.09 | 41.5% | 0.585 / 0.622 |
| 36 months | 193 | −1.372c | −3.87 | 29.0% | 0.634 / 0.699 |
| 60 months | 169 | −5.154c | −7.10† | 5.9% | 0.668 / 0.783 |
| 120 months | 109 | −29.319c | −28.65† | **0.0%** | 0.653 / 0.871 |

† **Read those two *t*'s as direction, not as size-correct tests.** The HAC lag truncation
is the horizon itself, which at 60 and 120 months is 36% and 110% of the window count; and
the sample holds only **3** independent 60-month programmes and **1** independent 120-month
programme. The *sign* and the equity-weight column are the informative part; the magnitude
of the *t* is not.

**Cross-check sleeves** — IEF −0.165c (*t* = −1.70, VA wins 48.7%, equity 0.674/0.688);
QQQ −3.469c (*t* = −5.04, VA wins 17.1%, equity 0.618/0.704). The damage scales with the
sleeve's drift and with the exposure shortfall, exactly as the mechanism predicts: on the
low-drift bond sleeve, where the flat path barely lags the market, the gap is ~zero.

## The decisive cut — exposure-matched, then placebo'd

Dial DCA's monthly purchase down by λ until both arms carry the same mean equity weight;
whatever survives is the contrarian *timing*, with the beta difference removed. **λ is
fitted IN-SAMPLE on this very tape** — the gap below is therefore an in-sample residual,
not an out-of-sample result. The placebo underneath is fitted exactly the same way on each
synthetic path, which is the only reason the two are comparable.

| | Value |
|---|--:|
| λ (bisected) | 0.8984 (residual exposure gap +0.0018) |
| Exposure-matched gap | **+0.702c** |
| HAC *t* / VA win rate | +3.05 / 72.5% |
| Bootstrap 95% CI | [+0.269, +1.078] |

So there *is* something — but it is not skill. Running the identical exposure-matched race
(same in-sample bisection, seeds 2000–2011) on **twelve** random walks calibrated to SPY's
own log-drift (0.1016), volatility (0.1979) and cash rate (0.0136), i.e. worlds with
**zero** predictability, produces a mean gap of **−0.249c** with sd **1.441** and a range
**[−2.838, +1.805]**.

| Placebo read on the real tape's +0.702c | Value |
|---|--:|
| z inside the no-predictability spread | **+0.66** |
| Zero-predictability worlds that beat it outright | **2 / 12** |
| Distribution-free one-sided *p* | **0.231** |

Buying the dips of a random walk earns a mechanical rebalancing bonus; nothing on this tape
exceeds it. Two caveats stated rather than buried: the placebo paths hold **volatility
constant**, whereas SPY's clusters — a vol-clustered tape would hand a contrarian schedule a
*larger* bonus, so this placebo if anything **understates** the null and the reading above is
the conservative one. And the placebo's cash leg is a **constant** rate fitted to BIL's
realised 19-year compound (1.36%/yr), not BIL's actual zero-then-five-percent path; both are
ASSUMPTIONS of the placebo, not of the headline.

## Synthetic control (machinery proof only — never supports the stamp)

- **Planted mean reversion** (transitory OU component, verified by a sub-one variance
  ratio): raw gap **+6.76c** (*t* = +5.00, VA wins 86.2%) over 30 years; exposure-matched
  on a 12-year tape **+8.19c** (*t* = +4.26). The harness finds a real contrarian edge
  when one is planted.
- **Zero-volatility null** (constant growth, nothing to trade against): exposure-matched
  gap **−0.11c**. Silent, as it must be.

## Verdict

- **Signal — None.** The claim that value averaging beats dollar-cost averaging does not
  hold on identical committed capital: **−1.372c per dollar contributed**, HAC *t* =
  **−3.87**, bootstrap CI entirely below zero, ahead in only **29.0%** of 193 programmes,
  negative in both eras, on both cross-check sleeves and at every horizon from 24 to 120
  months. Worse for the claim, the *sign* is set by a **non-tape assumption** — the value
  path's growth rate — which is functionally an equity-weight dial (0.634 invested at
  0%/yr, 0.693 at 12%/yr, against DCA's 0.699). Exposure-matched — on an **in-sample**
  λ — the residual +0.702c is indistinguishable from what a calibrated random walk pays
  (z = +0.66; 2 of 12 zero-predictability worlds beat it outright, one-sided *p* = 0.231),
  i.e. the rebalancing bonus rather than timing. The synthetic control recovers a planted wobble
  and is silent on a flat tape, so the miss belongs to the rule, not the harness.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** The advertised advantage exists only in the **equity-only
  IRR** (+0.92 pp/yr), a number that moves 18 bp across a buffer sweep over which the
  whole-programme IRR halves, and which is therefore incapable of describing the programme;
  at the 6-month default the whole-programme IRR is 10.07% against DCA's 10.64%. Costs are irrelevant — VA trades less notional than DCA and the
  gap barely moves at 25 bp. What is not irrelevant is the funding: **86.5%** of
  programmes are unfundable without a buffer, and even with six months in reserve the rule
  made a **3.3-contribution** call in a single month (**6.6** across that programme's
  binding months), in 2008.
- **Is there anything here?** One genuine, small thing: contrarian trading of a volatile
  sleeve harvests a rebalancing bonus, worth about +0.7c per dollar over 36 months when
  exposure is held equal. It is not specific to Edleson's rule, it does not require any
  forecasting ability, and it is smaller than the equity weight the rule silently gives up
  to obtain it.
